evals.prompt:
I'm setting up CompileIQ for a CUDA GEMM kernel and three of us need to pick what to pass as search_space= to Search():

(a) I only want to tune the PTXAS stage for the kernel.
(b) A colleague wants full-pipeline tuning with nvcc-level knobs, front-end included.
(c) Another colleague was sent a dev-build search space .bin file and just wants to try it as-is.

What should each of us pass, and is there anything to watch out for?
evals.expected_output: All three providers come from compileiq.search_spaces.compilers. (a) PtxasSearchSpace(), which by default fetches the latest PTXAS 13.3 'default' variant from GitHub releases; 'default' is the generic starting point and the right choice for a GEMM, not the attention-focused 'att' variant. (b) NvccSearchSpace(version="13.3") for full-compiler (front-end plus back-end) tuning. (c) LocalSearchSpaceBin("/path/to/file.bin"), which skips the manifest and the network; it only checks that the file exists and does not validate the .bin contents, so a malformed file fails later when the core parses it. Each is passed as Search(objective_function=..., search_space=ss, search_config=...).
assertions: Recommended PtxasSearchSpace with the default variant for the PTXAS-only GEMM case
Recommended NvccSearchSpace for full nvcc-pipeline tuning
Recommended LocalSearchSpaceBin with the file path for the one-off .bin, noting it skips the manifest and network
Warned that LocalSearchSpaceBin only checks the file exists and does not validate its contents

evals.prompt: We're publishing a paper with CompileIQ results and reviewers need to rerun exactly what we ran. Our script currently does `search_space=PtxasSearchSpace()`. Is that reproducible? If not, what should we change, and how do we see which search-space files a given release contains?
evals.expected_output: Not reproducible as written: PtxasSearchSpace() uses tag="latest", so it resolves to whatever the newest search-space release is at run time, and that can change. Pin all three selectors explicitly, for example PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="default", tag="search-spaces-...") with the concrete release tag you used. List the assets of a release with `gh release view --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' -R NVIDIA/CompileIQ <tag>`. Resolved binaries are cached under ~/.cache/compileiq/<tag>/ and verified by sha256, so a pinned tag gives the same file on every run.
assertions: Explained that the default tag is 'latest' and can resolve to a different release over time
Showed PtxasSearchSpace with version, variant and an explicit search-spaces-* tag pinned
Gave the gh release view command against NVIDIA/CompileIQ to enumerate a release's assets

evals.prompt: I'm tuning a FlashAttention-style grouped-query attention kernel with CompileIQ. I saw an 'att' variant for ptxas mentioned somewhere and assumed it means attribute-based register allocation, which doesn't sound relevant. Should I use it, or stick with the default ptxas search space?
evals.expected_output: Use it. 'att' is short for attention, not "attribute"; the attribute wording came from earlier docs that mislabeled the variant. The att variant (file ptxas13.3_att_search_space.bin) is curated for attention kernels such as FlashAttention, GQA, MHA, MLA and FlashInfer Batch Decode, and should be preferred whenever the kernel is attention-shaped. Select it with PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="att") and pass it as search_space= to Search(). The 'default' variant remains the starting point for generic, non-attention kernels.
assertions: Corrected the user: 'att' means attention, not attribute
Recommended the att variant for the GQA / FlashAttention kernel
Showed PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="att")
Noted that the default variant is the choice for non-attention kernels

evals.prompt: Can you review /workspace/input/tune_kernels.py before I merge it? It's our nightly CompileIQ tuning script and I want to make sure each kernel is getting the right search space. Point out anything wrong and show the corrected KERNEL_SEARCH_SPACES block.
evals.expected_output: Findings: (1) The comment is wrong: 'att' means attention, not attribute-based register allocation. (2) fused_gemm_bias_gelu and rmsnorm are not attention kernels, so they should use PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="default") (or just PtxasSearchSpace()). (3) gqa_decode is a GQA / FlashInfer-style batch decode attention kernel, so it should use PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="att"). (4) mla_prefill uses NvccSearchSpace(variant="att"), but the only NVCC variant available is 'default' (the att variant exists for ptxas 13.3 only); use PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="att") for MLA, or NvccSearchSpace(version="13.3") with the default variant if NVCC-level knobs are required. (5) paged_kv_copy feeds a Booster Pack .acf to LocalSearchSpaceBin; Booster Pack .acf files are pre-built candidates to apply outside a search, not search spaces, and LocalSearchSpaceBin does not validate contents, so this fails downstream. Apply the .acf directly, or run a fresh search with a real search space such as PtxasSearchSpace(). Optionally pin tag= for nightly reproducibility.
assertions: Read /workspace/input/tune_kernels.py
Flagged the comment: 'att' means attention, not attribute
Moved the GEMM and RMSNorm kernels to the default ptxas variant
Switched gqa_decode to PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3", variant="att")
Flagged NvccSearchSpace(variant="att") because NVCC only has a default variant
Flagged passing a Booster Pack .acf to LocalSearchSpaceBin as a misuse, since Booster Pack .acf files are applied outside a search

evals.prompt: Our GPU cluster has no outbound internet access. When I call PtxasSearchSpace().retrieve() on a compute node it hangs and then fails trying to reach GitHub. I do have a laptop with internet and can copy files onto the cluster's shared filesystem. How do I get CompileIQ working there?
evals.expected_output: Mirror the search-space release. On the connected machine, download the release's manifest plus all .bin files with `gh release download <tag> -R NVIDIA/CompileIQ -D <dir>`. Copy that directory to the cluster (rsync, scp, etc.), then on the compute node `export CIQ_SEARCH_SPACES_DIR=<dir>`. The providers then read manifest.json and the .bin files from that directory and skip the network. Verify with `python -c "from compileiq.search_spaces.compilers import PtxasSearchSpace; print(PtxasSearchSpace().retrieve())"`. A misconfigured mirror (for example a missing manifest) produces a clear error. If only one .bin is needed, LocalSearchSpaceBin(path) also works without the manifest.
assertions: Recommended downloading the release manifest and .bin files on a connected host with gh release download from NVIDIA/CompileIQ
Told the user to set CIQ_SEARCH_SPACES_DIR to the mirrored directory on the cluster
Stated that the mirror directory needs the manifest plus the .bin files
Suggested verifying with PtxasSearchSpace().retrieve()

evals.prompt: I want CompileIQ to tune my custom CUDA kernel's launch parameters and the PTXAS flags at the same time. The launch parameters are: BLOCK_SIZE from {64, 128, 256, 512}; NUM_STAGES an integer from 1 to 5; an ENABLE_PREFETCH flag that should normally be 1 but that the search is allowed to switch off; and a SCALE factor between 1e-3 and 1.0 that should be explored on a log scale with about 20 values. Write the search_space for me and tell me what my objective function will receive.
evals.expected_output:
Build the user-defined part from the primitives in compileiq.search_spaces.base and combine it with a compiler provider in a list:

    import compileiq.search_spaces.base as ss
    from compileiq.search_spaces.compilers import PtxasSearchSpace

    search_space = [
        {
            "BLOCK_SIZE": ss.choice([64, 128, 256, 512]),
            "NUM_STAGES": ss.range(start=1, end=5, step=1),
            "ENABLE_PREFETCH": ss.literal(1, knockout_prob=0.5),
            "SCALE": ss.log_sampling(start=1e-3, end=1.0, total=20),
        },
        PtxasSearchSpace(version="13.3"),
    ]

choice samples from a discrete list, range covers the integer span, literal with knockout_prob lets the GA disable the flag, and log_sampling gives 20 log-spaced buckets. Because the search space is a list, the objective receives a list of the same length, one entry per search-space element in the same order, so it must unpack both entries (compileiq-author-objective shows the unpacking pattern).
assertions: Used ss.choice for BLOCK_SIZE and ss.range for NUM_STAGES from compileiq.search_spaces.base
Used ss.literal with knockout_prob for the ENABLE_PREFETCH flag
Used ss.log_sampling with start, end and total for SCALE
Combined the user dict and PtxasSearchSpace in a list
Explained that the objective receives a list of the same length and must unpack it

evals.prompt: My CUDA kernel's occupancy is limited by register usage. What does the ptxas -maxrregcount option do, how do I pass it through nvcc, and what's the downside of setting it too low?
evals.expected_output: General CUDA advice: -maxrregcount caps the registers per thread that ptxas may allocate, which can raise occupancy. Pass it with `nvcc --maxrregcount=N` or `-Xptxas -maxrregcount=N` (or use __launch_bounds__ per kernel). Setting it too low forces register spills to local memory, which can slow the kernel. Check with -Xptxas -v and a profiler. Nothing CompileIQ-specific is needed.
assertions: Did not load or follow compileiq-search-space
Explained how to pass -maxrregcount through nvcc and the register-spill tradeoff

evals.prompt: Give me a shell one-liner that lists the 10 largest files under the current directory, recursively, with human-readable sizes.
evals.expected_output: A standard shell pipeline, for example `find . -type f -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -n 10`. Nothing CompileIQ-specific is needed.
assertions: Did not load or follow compileiq-search-space
Gave a working shell one-liner that lists the 10 largest files with human-readable sizes
